messages:
anya: Heads-up — nsys export from the nightly perf run has a ton of <unknown> frames for CUDA kernels. Trace uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/nightlies/1795506781.nsys
perf-bot: profiling job finished: /traces/1795506781.nsys (480MB) :white_check_mark:
jun: did you run inside the same container we use in staging? Missing symbols often come from stripped binaries or CUPTI/CUDA mismatches. :thinking:
matt: can you paste the Dockerfile final stage + build flags you used?
anya: short excerpt from the final image (we use multi-stage):
```
FROM gcr.io/distroless/cc
COPY --from=builder /app/serving_runtime /app/serving_runtime
RUN strip --strip-all /app/serving_runtime
```
We're definitely stripping the binary in release image.
jun: yep that will remove DWARF and much of the symbol table. nsys needs either symbol table or a binary built with -g and exported symbols (-rdynamic) to show function names/line info.
anya: what's the recommended compile flags for profiling builds?
matt: for profiling/debug image we use minimal optimization and keep frame pointers + dynamic symbols. Example: 
```
CXXFLAGS="-g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer -rdynamic"
LDFLAGS="-Wl,--enable-new-dtags"
```
and do not run strip. Also keep libc++/libstdc++ debug syms if possible.
ci-bot: FYI our current build matrix has PROFILE=true which sets -g, but it's only used in the unit-test matrix, not the docker image pipeline.
jun: another frequent root cause: CUPTI inside the container doesn't match the host CUDA or is missing dependencies. nsys/CUPTI will silently fall back and you'll see anonymous frames. Run these checks inside the runtime container: 
```
file /app/serving_runtime
readelf -Ws /app/serving_runtime | head -n 20
ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcupti.so
nsys status || true
```

anya: ran the checks in the container, got this for ldd:
```
$ ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcupti.so
\tlibcuda.so.1 => not found
```
The distroless final image doesn't have CUDA libs available. That explains a lot.
matt: that will definitely break CUPTI hooks. If CUPTI can't bind to libcuda it can fail to expose symbol info for kernels. Quick options:
- produce a profiling image that keeps /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI and required CUDA libs (or mount them at runtime)
- don't strip profiling binaries (keep -g, -rdynamic)
- ensure the CUPTI library version matches the driver/CUDA on the node

jun: I'll add a small diagnostic checklist we can paste to runbook: 
1) Confirm binary has symbols: `file /app/serving_runtime` -> "not stripped" and `readelf -Ws` shows exported symbols.
2) Confirm dynamic symbols visible: `readelf -s /app/serving_runtime | grep <kernel_entry_name>`
3) Confirm CUPTI linkage: `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcupti.so` -> no missing deps.
4) Confirm nsys can attach: `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=nvtx --output=tmp ./serving_runtime`
5) Open the produced `.qdrep` in Nsight / Perfetto and check kernel names/times.

anya: I rebuilt a debug profiling image (kept -g -rdynamic, removed strip step) and mounted the node's /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI into the container. Re-ran nsys — kernel names and stack frames are now resolved. Tests look good locally.
matt: :tada: nice catch. If CUPTI symbols are present the trace shows `my_kernel_name` instead of `<unknown>`.
jun: let's also make CI fail early: add a tiny nsys smoke step that profiles a short synthetic job and asserts that unknown frames < 20% or that at least N kernels have a resolved symbol. That prevents regressions in the Dockerfile and build matrix.
anya: opened PR #1823 to: add PROFILE=true pipeline image, stop stripping in that image, mount CUPTI in the profiling job, and include the nsys smoke check with minimal runtime. Linked repro script too.
ci-bot: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1823 (ci checks queued)
matt: will review today, small nit on the smoke script paths then ship.
anya: thanks — this saved a full day of blind debugging. I'll add the diagnostic checklist to the eng-runtime runbook.
